title: region-mesh-shadowing-and-conditional-data-locks
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a region-mesh placement and failover subsystem for Dedicated fleets that supports heterogeneous hardware affinity, capacity shadowing (traffic mirroring to standby zones), and conditional data locks for short-term residency constraints. This will allow customers to specify fine-grained placement intent (preferred zone list, hardware affinity, residency windows) and enable orchestrated failover where standby capacity is warmed and traffic is shadowed before cutover to meet latency SLOs and data-residency constraints.

Goals:
- Allow Dedicated customers to declare a region-level placement policy with optional ordered zone affinity, explicit hardware class preferences (e.g., A100 vs H100), and temporal residency locks (time-windowed restrictions on moving state out of a zone).
- Provide 'capacity shadowing' that mirrors a controlled percentage of production traffic to failover zones to prewarm caches/KV and validate model variant compatibility without serving responses to end users.
- Implement 'conditional data-locks' which prevent or require operator approval for state movement when requests touch residency-sensitive tokens, with audit trail.
- Ensure autoscaling policies and throughput guarantees honor placement constraints and do not violate data residency.

Acceptance criteria:
- API: Customers can create/update a placement policy via Dedicated config with: preferred_zones (ordered list), hardware_affinity (list), residency_windows (list of date-ranges or cron-like spec), shadow_percentage (0-20), and lock_behavior (block | require-approval | allow-after-warmup).
- Orchestrator: Scheduler honors policies during initial placement, scale-up, and node drain. If shadow_percentage>0, scheduler establishes mirrored request path and metrics collection without promoting mirrored responses.
- Failover: Automated failover only promotes standby zone after shadowing health checks pass (latency, kv-hit-rate, model-output-consistency) or after manual approval when conditional data-locks are active.
- Observability: Console surfaces per-fleet: shadowing ratio, shadow success rate, residency-locked request count, prewarm cache hit-rate, and the timeline of any promoted failover with audit logs.
- Tests: End-to-end chaos test demonstrates region failover with zero lost requests under a steady-state workload sample, and a separate test shows the orchestrator blocks promotion when conditional-data-lock denies move.

Technical approach:
1) Policy model: introduce a placement_policy object in Dedicated fleet spec. It is validated on create/update and persisted to the control plane. The schema includes metadata for residency windows and a 'lock_signature' to record approvals.
2) Shadowing path: extend the proxy layer to support mirrored request copies routed to standby nodes. Mirrors are processed by the same runtime but responses are dropped; telemetry is recorded. Mirror path uses dedicated bandwidth cap to avoid interfering with production SLOs.
3) Warmup metrics: define heuristic health gates (kv_cache_hit_rate >= X, average token-latency <= Y ms, model-determinism score >= Z) for promotion. These are configurable per-customer.
4) Conditional data-locks: when a request touches flagged tokens/indicators (e.g., enterprise data tags), mark the associated session as residency-locked. Locked sessions cannot be moved until lock expires or operator approves. All lock state is recorded in audit log with user/timestamp.
5) Scheduler changes: modify placement algorithm to prefer nodes matching hardware_affinity and to avoid violating residency_windows during scheduled drains or autoscale shrink. Implement a 'grace leash' where nodes cannot be forcibly moved during the leash period without escalation.
6) Autoscale integration: autoscaler respects placement constraints; scale-out will attempt to allocate within preferred zones first, then fallback to secondary zones only if policy allows. Scale-in must ensure no locked sessions are evicted; otherwise it stalls or triggers operator workflow.
7) Rollout strategy: feature-flagged rollout. Phase 1 enable policy creation and dry-run planning; Phase 2 enable shadowing for selected fleets; Phase 3 enable automatic promotion for fleets with no residency locks, keep manual approval for fleets with locks.

Rollout plan and timeline:
- Week 1-2: API/schema + basic scheduler hooks (dry-run only). Unit tests + schema validation.
- Week 3: Mirror/Shadow path implementation in proxy and lightweight telemetry. Internal e2e on staging.
- Week 4: Conditional data-lock primitives + audit trail + UI views. Add operator approval flow.
- Week 5: Autoscaler integration and chaos experiments (simulate zone failure).
- Week 6: Pilot with 2 customers and gradual ramp to GA by week 8.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Shadow-success-rate >= 95% within 10 minutes of shadow start.
- Prewarm-latency-p95 for promoted zone <= production p95 * 1.2.
- No promoted failover without passing health gates unless manual override used.
- Residency-lock audit entries must be persisted within 5s of lock event.

Operational runbooks and playbooks:
- Play for a failed promotion: rollback routing, revert to previous active zone, and open incident vaccum with frozen autoscale.
- Play for stuck scale-in due to locks: notify customer and open an approval ticket; if customer does not respond in SLA, put a hold and offer temporary burst capacity in allowed regions.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- Existing Dedicated fleets default to legacy placement behavior unless placement_policy is present.
- Migration tooling will produce a dry-run plan that simulates placement decisions under the new scheduler and surfaces any conflicts with residency_windows.

Security & compliance notes:
- Conditional-data-lock requires HSM-backed signatures on operator approvals.
- Audit trail must be exportable in CSV/JSON for compliance review.
- Work with privacy and legal on residency window semantics for cross-border regulatory requirements.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define deterministic 'model-determinism' metric across model families? (Research/Applied ML input required.)
- Bandwidth/cost trade-offs for shadowing traffic at scale. Proposal: cap mirror bandwidth per fleet to a configurable MB/s.
- UX for customers to express complex residency policies (cron vs specific dates). Need PM/Design iteration.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DED/pages/Regional+Mesh+Design (draft)
- GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-scheduler/pull/312 (WIP)
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-DRIVE/region-mesh-mocks

Success metrics post-GA:
- 60% of new Dedicated fleets adopt placement_policy when they have multi-zone requirements.
- Mean time to failover (after health gates pass) <= 45s for pilot fleets.
- No compliance-related incidents attributable to automatic promotions in first 6 months.

Acceptance sign-off:
- PM: product-runbook review completed.
- Security: conditional-data-lock pattern and HSM flow approved.
- SRE: chaos experiments pass.
comments: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, and Applied ML. Decided to cap shadow traffic at 10% for initial pilot. Action: design API schema (Sofia).

2026-03-03: Scheduler dry-run implemented. Mateo: dry-run shows 97% placement success within preferred zones for our internal sim. Noted edge-case where residency_window crosses timezone boundary — need normalization. (PR #312).

2026-03-08: Proxy mirror path prototype demonstrates warm cache hit-rate improvements in standby zone after 15 minutes of 5% shadow traffic. Telemetry integrated into Console mockups. UX review scheduled with Design.

2026-03-12: Security review: conditional-data-locks accepted with HSM-signed approvals and operator audit record. SRE requested additional metric for 'lock_eviction_attempts' — added to monitoring TODO. Ready to start pilot onboarding checklist.
